title: The best of all ways
hook: the highest dharma is to repeat the Name and do pure deeds (Sukhmani 3)

segments.voice: Yesterday, beyond every pilgrimage, and your line: simple and sincere. Did you do your small thing all the way? This is a week's end: the breaker of pain, the door, the road, the companion, the many scriptures. Today, what the third ashtpadi puts first. Day four hundred forty-eight.
screen: `SIMPLE AND SINCERE.` · `A WEEK: PAIN BROKEN, THE ROAD, THE SCRIPTURES.`

segments.voice: After a long list of what doesn't measure up, a reader wants to know: so what does? Yesterday's stanzas set fasting, pilgrimage, ritual and learning beside the Name, one by one. If you stopped there, you might think the third ashtpadi was only a list of no. But it ends with a list of yes. The last stanza is built like a ladder of superlatives: of all the ways, this one; of all the efforts, this one; of all the places, this one. And its first line is one Sikhs often quote.
screen: `SO WHAT DOES MEASURE UP?` → `A LIST OF NO, THEN A LIST OF YES.` → `A LADDER: OF ALL..., THIS ONE.`

segments.voice: It begins: sarab dharam meh sresht dharam, har ko naam jap nirmal karam. Sarab: all. Dharam: a way of right living, a duty, a practice. Sresht: highest, best. So: of all ways of right living, the highest is to chant the Name of God and do pure deeds. Nirmal means spotless, without dirt. Karam means action. A word about dharam. In Gurbani it usually doesn't mean a religion as an institution. It means duty, righteousness, the way a person ought to live. So the line isn't a contest between faiths. It's a statement about what a good life is made of: two things, held together. Remembering, and clean action. Then the ladder goes on, in paraphrase. Of all rites, the highest is the company of the holy, which washes away evil thinking. Of all efforts, the best is to chant the Name of God, always. Of all speech, the nectar is to hear God's praise and speak it with your tongue. Of all places, the highest is the heart in which the Name of God dwells. Notice where the ladder ends. Not in a temple. Not on a mountain. In a heart. After all the pilgrimages of yesterday, the best place turns out to be the one you're carrying around. And notice what comes paired with the Name at the very top: nirmal karam, pure deeds. Remembering alone isn't the whole of it. It has to show up in what you do.
screen: `SARAB DHARAM: OF ALL WAYS OF LIVING.` · `THE NAME, AND SPOTLESS ACTION.` · `HOLY COMPANY, GOD'S PRAISE.` · `THE HIGHEST PLACE: A HEART.` · then, large: `NAME AND PURE DEEDS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: do one pure deed. Pure here means clean: no angle, no audience, no score kept. Sit and let one come to mind. Pay a compliment you mean and expect nothing back. Return something you borrowed. Pick up litter no one will thank you for. Fix the thing someone else broke without mentioning it. Choose one, and picture doing it simply. If you pray, say Waheguru once, letting the Name and the deed sit side by side. The bell holds the time.

The best of all ways. The last stanza of Sukhmani's third ashtpadi: of all ways of right living, the highest is to chant the Name and do pure deeds, and the highest place is a heart where the Name lives.
screen: `THE BEST OF ALL WAYS — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: name and pure deeds. Today, do the clean deed you chose, and keep it to yourself. Day four hundred forty-eight.

howItsDone: Sikhs reading Sukhmani recite this stanza at the end of the third ashtpadi; its opening line about the Name and pure deeds is often quoted in Sikh teaching and sung as a shabad.

match.prompt: the ladder of the last stanza — tap the pairs.
pairs: a heart where the Name dwells

myth: dharam in this line means one religion versus others
in Gurbani it usually means right living, duty, the way one ought to live.
nirmal karam means spotless, pure action
the line pairs it with chanting the Name.
the stanza names a holy city as the highest place
the highest place is the heart in which the Name dwells.

fork.setup: after a long list of efforts that don't equal the Name, the third ashtpadi names the highest way. what is it?
options: chanting the Name and doing pure deeds.
fork.reveal: sarab dharam meh sresht dharam, har ko naam jap nirmal karam: the Name and spotless action, together.

original.note: Gurmukhi: dharam, right living, duty; the line names the highest dharam.

trapdoor: what you thought: the best of all ways means the best religion.
what it means: of all ways of right living, the highest is remembering the Name together with pure action.
what a scholar hears: the pauri is built on 'sagal ... meh' superlatives (dharam, kiriaa, udam, baanee, thaan), ending in the ghat, the heart, where naam dwells.

sources.ref: Gauri Sukhmani M5, ashtpadi 3, pauri 8, Ang 266

notes: Pauri 8 transliterated 'sarab dharam meh sresht dharam, har ko naam jap nirmal karam' and the rest paraphrased (of all rites, holy company washing away evil thinking; of all efforts, chanting the Name; of all speech, hearing and speaking God's praise; of all places, the heart where the Name dwells). Confirm.
